introduction_markdown:
Answer both questions beginning each answer on a new page in the answer booklet. Both answers carry equal marks.

Credit will be given for accuracy, correct use of a variety of expressions, verbs, vocabulary and idioms.

Use blue ink only.

You are reminded of the necessity for orderly presentation of your answers.
enonce_intro_markdown:
*Using a tense suitable to your chosen topic, write an essay in French, of at least 140 and not more than 150 words, (not counting figures, words in brackets, abbreviations and names of people or places) on ONE of the following topics.*

*Credit will be given for the correct use of a variety of expressions, verbs, vocabulary and idioms.*

*If you choose topic (b), your name must be Yaka and your address Lycee de Kombo.*

*If you choose topic (c), your essay must be based on the events in the picture.*

*Off-topic material will earn no marks.*

questions.enonce_markdown:
(c) Racontez une histoire basée sur les images ci-dessous en vous appuyant sur l'adage « l'eau c'est la vie ». Dans votre histoire,

- dites ce que les gens font dans ces images ;
- parlez des problèmes d'eau potable dans votre localité
- et proposez des solutions pour le résoudre.

![fig-1](gce-ol-french-2019-p2-officiel-cameroun_exercice_2c_fig_1.png)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**The three pictures, in order**

- **A.** A dry, cracked ground (a drought); a person bends over the cracks in the earth, apparently looking for water.
- **B.** Two people kneel in a hollow dug in the dry ground and scoop up water with their hands and a container; plastic containers stand beside them.
- **C.** A long line of women walks across a dry plain, each carrying a jar or a bucket on her head, going to fetch water far away.

**Tense chosen:** the present tense. The topic asks the candidate to say what the people do in the pictures, to speak about the water problems of the locality and to propose solutions, so the present is the natural tense for describing the pictures and stating a general situation, and the future is used for the result of the solutions.

**Model essay** (141 words)

« L'eau, c'est la vie », dit un vieil adage, et les images le prouvent. Sur la première image, la terre est sèche et couverte de fentes, car il n'a pas plu depuis des mois. Sur la deuxième, une femme et un enfant creusent un trou dans le sol pour trouver un peu d'eau boueuse qu'ils versent dans des bidons. Sur la troisième, de nombreuses femmes marchent en file sous le soleil, avec des jarres sur la tête, pour aller chercher de l'eau très loin.

Dans notre localité aussi, l'eau potable manque cruellement. Les villageois boivent une eau sale et beaucoup tombent malades.

Pour résoudre ce problème, il faut construire des forages et des puits équipés de pompes. Les habitants doivent aussi protéger les sources et entretenir ensemble les points d'eau. Ainsi, tout le monde aura de l'eau propre près de chez soi.

**Notes**

The essay covers the three points of the topic: what the people do in the pictures (first paragraph, pictures A, B and C), the drinking-water problems of the locality (second paragraph) and solutions (third paragraph), and it is built on the adage *l'eau, c'est la vie*. Picture A is read as a drought and picture B as people digging for water; these are interpretations of grey, partly obscured photographs.

**Marking criteria**

| Criterion | What earns the marks |
|---|---|
| Accuracy | Correct verb forms, agreements, spelling and accents; correct use of the tense chosen |
| Variety of expressions | Linking words (*d'abord*, *puis*, *finalement*, *heureusement*) and set phrases |
| Variety of verbs | Several different verbs instead of *être*, *avoir* and *faire* only |
| Vocabulary and idioms | Words and expressions suited to the topic; idioms used correctly |
| Relevance and length | All the points of the topic covered; between 140 and 150 words |

**Common mistakes**

1. Not following the pictures, or leaving out one of the three points (what the people do, the water problems of the locality, the solutions). Off-topic material earns no marks.
2. Describing each picture one by one ("Sur l'image A...") without a link between them and without the adage, instead of building a connected account.
